samples.summary: `DELETE .../tabs/:tabId` bypasses the new `safeWorksheetRecordKeys` tab guard: `resolveDelete` still tests truthiness of `root.tabs?.[tabId]`
samples.evidence: This change introduces `findWorksheet`/`worksheetOrThrow` (worksheet-lookup.util.ts) precisely because `root.sheets[tabId]`/`root.tabs[tabId]` answer TRUTHY for non-tab keys — `Object.prototype` for `__proto__` on a plain root, and a *function* for `toJSON`/`getID`/`toString` on a live Yorkie object proxy. The new `duplicate` handler adopts the guard (`tabs.controller.ts:270`: `if (!safeWorksheetRecordKeys(root.tabs).includes(tabId)) throw NotFound`), but the new `remove` handler (`tabs.controller.ts:172`) goes through `resolveDelete`, which is still `const tab = root.tabs?.[tabId]; if (!tab) return not_found` (tab-ops.ts:78-79). `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/W/documents/D/tabs/toJSON` therefore passes the not_found check on a live document and reaches `applyDelete` (tab-ops.ts:102-106) inside `doc.update`, which runs `delete root.tabs['toJSON']` and `delete root.sheets['toJSON']` — Yorkie's object proxy routes `delete` to `RHTPQMap.deleteByKey`, which throws `fail to find <key>` for a key that was never set (this diff's own comment-ops.ts:308-312 documents exactly that behaviour). Result: a 500 out of the middle of a CRDT transaction instead of a 404. On any non-proxy/plain root the same request instead returns HTTP 200 `{ id: '__proto__', name: undefined, deleted: true }` for a tab that never existed. `resolveMove` is safe (it uses `tabOrder.indexOf`), so `remove` is the one hole.

samples.summary: `listThreads` walks the comment map with raw `Object.keys`, the exact call that `safeWorksheetRecordKeys` exists to survive
samples.evidence: `listThreads` does `for (const id of Object.keys(map))` on what is, in production, a live Yorkie `JSONObject` proxy. worksheet-lookup.util.ts:29-34 (added in this change) states that `ownKeys` throws `TypeError: ... duplicate` on a record that ended up with duplicate CRDT keys, and that raw `Object.keys` is therefore unusable — which is why every other record walk in the backend goes through `safeWorksheetRecordKeys`/`safeWorksheetRecordEntries`. On such a document `GET .../comments` (and `tabIdOfThread`, which calls `findThread` per tab) would 500 rather than list. `ApiV1WorksheetImagesController.getImages` (worksheet-images.controller.ts:63) has the same exposure via `Object.values(ws.images)`.

samples.summary: An unknown `layoutId` is silently substituted with the first built-in layout instead of being rejected
samples.evidence: `addSlide` passes `layoutId` straight to `MemSlidesStore.addSlide`, whose `resolveLayout` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:172-174) is `this.doc.layouts.find(...) ?? getLayout(layoutId)`, and `getLayout` (packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:196-198) is `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS.find(...) ?? BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0]` — it never fails. So `POST .../slides {"layoutId":"typo"}` answers 200 and creates a slide with a layout the caller did not ask for, and the response (`{id, index, slideCount}`) does not report which layout was used. The controller only validates that `layoutId` is a non-empty string (slides.controller.ts:100), and the new `GET .../layouts` endpoint is offered as the discovery mechanism, so the mismatch is silently absorbed rather than surfaced.

samples.summary: `PATCH .../comments/:threadId` (resolve) and the reply route return a sheet thread whose anchor is missing the derived `ref` that `GET`/`POST` include
samples.evidence: `createThread` (line 337) and `list` (line 241) both run sheet threads through `withSref(...)`, which attaches the derived A1 `ref` to the `sheet-cell` anchor. `setResolved` returns `updated` straight from `mutateThread` (line 393-406) with no `withSref`, so the same thread comes back with `anchor` = `{kind,tabId,rowId,colId}` and no `ref`. A client that reads `thread.anchor.ref` after a resolve — which every read path teaches it to do — gets `undefined`, indistinguishable from the `null` that means "orphaned".

samples.summary: A thread whose comment list is empty can never be deleted through the API — the authorize step 404s on its own missing root comment
samples.evidence: `deleteThread`'s authorize callback computes `rootCommentId(thread)` = `copyThread(thread).comments[0]?.id`, which is `undefined` for a thread with zero comments; `assertCommentAuthor` (line 530-531) then does `const comment = commentId ? findComment(...) : undefined; if (!comment) throw new NotFoundException('Comment not found')`. `isThread` (comment-ops.ts:154-159) accepts an array-like of length 0, so such a thread is listable by `GET .../comments` but permanently undeletable — the API reports 404 for something it just returned.

samples.summary: `applySlideChange` move-to-front falls through to `moveAfterByIndex(-1, from)` when an array exposes `moveAfterByIndex` but not `moveFront`
samples.evidence: The branch is `if (slides.moveAfterByIndex && slides.getElementByIndex) { if (to === 0 && slides.moveFront) {...} else if (to > from) {...} else { slides.moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from); } }`. With `to === 0` and no `moveFront`, control reaches the final `else` and calls `moveAfterByIndex(-1, from)`. The frontend equivalent (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:831-837) branches on `clamped === 0` unconditionally and never produces a negative index. The plain-array splice fallback is only selected when `moveAfterByIndex` is absent entirely, so this shape is not covered by it.

samples.summary: `parsePdfAnchor` validates each of x/y/w/h in 0..1 independently but never that the rectangle stays on the page
samples.evidence: The loop only checks `value < 0 || value > 1` per field, so `{x: 0.9, y: 0.9, w: 1, h: 1}` is accepted and stores a region that extends to 1.9 of the page in both axes. The docblock states the coordinates are "page-relative 0..1", which the stored anchor then violates; the editor's PDF renderer will draw a highlight running off the page.

samples.summary: `notify` is documented as fire-and-forget but is fully awaited, so every comment write blocks on N notification DB round-trips
samples.evidence: The docblock (line 182-188) says "Fire-and-forget, exactly like `notifyCommentEvent` in the frontend", but the implementation is `for (const plan of plans) { await this.notificationService.createFromComment(...) }` and every caller does `await this.notify(...)` before returning (lines 309, 341, 372, 404). The failure isolation is correct (each call is try/caught), but the latency characteristic the comment claims is not what the code does.

finding.evidence: This change introduces `findWorksheet`/`worksheetOrThrow` (worksheet-lookup.util.ts) precisely because `root.sheets[tabId]`/`root.tabs[tabId]` answer TRUTHY for non-tab keys — `Object.prototype` for `__proto__` on a plain root, and a *function* for `toJSON`/`getID`/`toString` on a live Yorkie object proxy. verdict.reason: Verified in-tree. `remove` (tabs.controller.ts:161-197) resolves the tab solely via `resolveDelete`, whose check is the plain truthiness test `const tab = root.tabs?.[tabId]; if (!tab) return not_found` (tab-ops.ts:78-79) — no `safeWorksheetRecordKeys`/`findWorksheet` membership check on this path. The sibling `duplicate` handler in the same file adopted the guard at tabs.controller.ts:259 with a comment stating that `tabs['__proto__']` (plain root) and `tabs['toJSON']` (live Yorkie proxy) are both truthy, and worksheet-lookup.util.ts:4-34 documents the same hazard, so the repo itself asserts the truthiness test is insufficient. Past the check, `applyDelete` performs an unconditional `delete root.tabs[tabId]` (tab-ops.ts:103); comment-ops.ts:308-312 and comment-ops.spec.ts:154-162 document that Yorkie routes `delete` to `RHTPQMap.deleteByKey`, which throws `fail to find <key>` for a key never set — a 500 raised inside `doc.update` instead of a 404. On a plain root the same request returns 200 `{deleted:true}` for a nonexistent tab. No upstream guard filters `:tabId` (assertSheetDocument at tabs.controller.ts:55-62 validates only the document), and grep shows tabs.controller.ts:172 is the only non-test caller of `resolveDelete`. Real, reachable, and in the correctness lane (missing guard / wrong condition causing a crash on a live path).

searchedFor: read worksheet-charts.controller.ts, tabs.controller.ts, comments.controller.ts write paths
finding.summary: The new `assertPlainTabId` guard is applied in only one of ~8 controllers that do the identical `root.sheets?.[tabId]` lookup-then-write; the sibling routes still reach the write it protects
finding.evidence: `worksheet-images.controller.ts` now calls `assertPlainTabId(tabId)` in `worksheetOrThrow` (line 82) and in `getImages` (line 95), on the reasoning in its own docblock that on a plain (non-proxy) root `sheets['__proto__']` answers `Object.prototype`, so the NotFound guard passes and the subsequent `ws.images = {}` lands on the prototype. Every sibling controller has the byte-identical shape with no guard: `worksheet-charts.controller.ts:49` `worksheetOrThrow` → `:106-110` `ws.charts = {}; ws.charts[chart.id] = chart;`, `worksheet-styles.controller.ts:54/69/112`, `worksheet-dimensions.controller.ts:57/114/142/159/187/204/232/249/277`, `worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:47/62/110`, `cells.controller.ts:88/125/158/193/230`, and `comments.controller.ts:323` (guard) → `:330` `const ws = root.sheets[tabId]` inside `doc.update`. If the hazard the guard exists for is real, it is reachable through all of those routes; if it is not real, the guard is unnecessary. Either way the codebase is now inconsistent and the protected operation is bypassable at the cited call sites.

verdict.reason: The finding searched for a symbol name (`assertPlainTabId`) that does not exist anywhere in the repo, and concluded the guard was absent from the siblings. The guard actually exists as a shared util: `worksheet-lookup.util.ts:36-59` defines `findWorksheet`/`worksheetOrThrow`, whose docblock (lines 4-35) describes precisely the hazard the finding attributes to it and closes it with a membership test over `safeWorksheetRecordKeys`. The counterexample is in the finding's own titled file: `worksheet-charts.controller.ts:88` calls `worksheetOrThrow(root, tabId)` on the line immediately preceding `ws.charts = {}` (:91), and the read path is guarded at :68 — the cited lines :49/:106-110 do not exist in that 99-line file. Every other sibling named as unguarded also applies the util on both read and write paths: worksheet-styles :53/:79/:97/:120, worksheet-dimensions :98/:118/:141/:161/:184/:204/:227/:247, worksheet-filter-pivot :46/:72/:92/:119, cells :89/:125/:158/:192/:228, and comments :329/:333 (both the pre-check and the in-doc.update write, on the caller-supplied body tabId). The only remaining raw `root.sheets?.[tabId]` reads, comments.controller.ts:238 and :562-567, take tabId from document-internal sources (`root.tabOrder` at :237; `tabIdOfThread(...)` at :560 with a NotFound at :561), never from URL or request body, so they are not bypass paths. The claimed inconsistency and bypassable write do not exist.
